questions.prompt: On a map of the world, which direction is at the top?
questions.explanation: The top of every world map is the north, which is why Italy, drawn above Tunisia, is north of it. The south is at the bottom, the east on the right and the west on the left.

questions.prompt: In Japan, how do people greet each other?

options.text: They shake hands with each other.
They kiss each other on the cheek.

questions.explanation: In Japan people bow: they bend the head and the back, and they do not touch. Shaking hands is the greeting of England and the USA, the kiss on the cheek belongs to Tunisia, France and Spain, and touching noses and foreheads is the Maori greeting of New Zealand.

questions.prompt: Complete: "My uncle travels ___ plane every month."
questions.explanation: A means of transport always takes by, with no little word behind it: travel by plane, by train, by car, by boat. The word to belongs to the place you go to, and in and on put you inside or above the plane instead of naming the way you travel.

questions.prompt: Which pair of little words is correct?
questions.explanation: The word egg begins with the vowel e, so it takes an; the word cape begins with the consonant c, so it takes a. The choice never comes from the meaning, only from the first letter of the word that follows.

questions.prompt: Big Ben was finished in 1859 and the Eiffel Tower in 1889. Complete: "Big Ben is ___ the Eiffel Tower."
questions.explanation: Two monuments are compared, so the short adjective takes -er and the second one follows than: Big Ben is older than the Eiffel Tower, because 1859 comes before 1889. A short English adjective never takes more in front of it, and the ending -est is for one thing above a whole group.
